Lint an Evidence Table

Source: R/lint_evidence.R
lint_evidence.Rd

Checks an evidence table against the R4SUB evidence schema and a handful of structural best practices, and reports every issue it finds at once as a tidy data.frame. This is the non-fatal counterpart to validate_evidence(): where validate_evidence() throws on the first problem (and is the right gate before scoring), lint_evidence() never throws on a malformed table, so you can see the full picture of what is wrong in one pass.

Usage

lint_evidence(ev, checks = NULL)

Arguments

ev

A data.frame to lint. It need not be a valid evidence table; that is the point.

checks

Optional character vector of check codes to run (see the codes in the descriptions above). The default, NULL, runs them all. Unknown codes are rejected.

Value

A tibble with one row per issue and the columns code (the check that fired), level (error, warning, or note), field (the column the issue concerns, or NA for a table-level issue), n (the number of rows affected, or NA for a table-level issue), and message (a human-readable description). A clean table returns a zero-row tibble with those columns. Rows are ordered most serious first. The result carries a "summary" attribute: a named integer vector counting findings at each level.

Details

Every check is structural. The linter reuses the schema from evidence_schema() and the version machinery behind evidence_schema_version(); it invents no scoring, weights, thresholds, or controlled vocabularies of its own, and it never judges whether a finding is good or bad for a submission. The checks are:

error

Issues that would also make validate_evidence() fail: a required column missing (missing_required_column), a schema column of the wrong type (wrong_type), an NA in a non-nullable column (na_in_required), a value outside a column's controlled vocabulary (invalid_value), or a schema-version stamp this release does not know (unknown_schema_version).

warning

A schema-version stamp older than the current one (outdated_schema_version), or an evidence_payload cell that is neither empty nor valid JSON (invalid_payload_json).

note

No schema-version stamp at all (missing_schema_version); more than one row sharing an (indicator_id, asset_id) key, which evidence_diff() would collapse (duplicate_key); a metric_value with no metric_unit (metric_value_without_unit) or a metric_unit with no metric_value (metric_unit_without_value).

See also

validate_evidence() for the strict gate, and evidence_schema() for the schema the checks are drawn from.

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
ev <- suppressMessages(as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "validation", asset_id = "ADSL",
    source_name = "pinnacle21", indicator_id = "SD0001",
    indicator_name = "SD0001", indicator_domain = "quality",
    severity = "high", result = "fail",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
))
# A valid table lints clean.
lint_evidence(ev)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 5
#> # ℹ 5 variables: code <chr>, level <chr>, field <chr>, n <int>, message <chr>

# A hand-built table with problems reports them all at once.
bad <- data.frame(
  run_id = "R1", study_id = "S1", asset_type = "dataset",
  asset_id = "ADSL", source_name = "x", indicator_id = "I1",
  indicator_name = "I1", indicator_domain = "quality",
  severity = "sky-high", result = "pass",
  created_at = Sys.time(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
lint_evidence(bad)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   code                   level field        n message                           
#>   <chr>                  <chr> <chr>    <int> <chr>                             
#> 1 invalid_value          error severity     1 Column 'severity' has value(s) ou…
#> 2 missing_schema_version note  NA          NA Evidence table has no schema-vers…
